what_worked: Data-quality caveat on the 56% untagged MRR is genuinely useful and disciplines every downstream claim.
fix_next: Total revenue is $15.6M not $13.47M; conflating MRR with 30-day revenue corrupts the headline metric and cascades through concentration and category figures.
verdict: Strong strategic narrative undermined by a core metric confusion between MRR and 30-day revenue.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2/3: States total MRR is $13.47M—the dataset total 30-day revenue is $15,596,344.59; the deck then separately quotes $15.6M as '30-day run-rate' and claims ~40% acceleration, but these are the same metric, making the acceleration narrative fabricated or at minimum unsupported. Slide 5: Top-10 share stated as 48.0%; reference is 49.6%—minor but directionally low. Slide 7: AI total shown as $1,806K; reference is $2,356K. Other category totals (SaaS $589K vs $703K, Education $524K vs $523K, Marketing $444K vs $1,317K) are materially off for Marketing especially. Slide 8: Education median shown as $2,142; reference is $2,435. AI median shown as $446; reference is $503. Slide 10: B2B median stated as $1,036 implying 5.7x B2C ($181); reference multiples are ~2.3x for medians—the 5.7x claim is substantially overstated. Slide 12: Stripe share stated as 87.2% of MRR; by revenue reference Stripe is $13.5M/$15.6M ≈ 86.7%—close but the denominator confusion persists.

evidence.insight: Slide 6 data-quality finding (56% untagged MRR) is an original, decision-useful insight that reframes all category analysis. Slide 9 portfolio matrix and slide 13 white-space analysis synthesize multiple dimensions. Slide 15 prioritization framework translates findings into sequenced actions.
evidence.narrative: Clear five-finding thesis on slide 2 carried through concentration (slide 5), data quality (slide 6), category (slides 7-9), B2B/B2C (slide 10), infrastructure (slide 12), risk (slide 14), and recommendations (slides 15-16). Each slide builds on prior findings. Strong landing with tiered recommendations.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 states audience (Senior Leadership), scope (1,000-listing sample), and date. Slide 6 explicitly scopes all category claims to the 44% tagged subset. Slide 14 acknowledges data incompleteness. Missing: no explicit limitations section on sample representativeness or cross-sectional nature.
evidence.accuracy: Core confusion: $13.47M labeled 'Total MRR' vs $15.6M '30-day run-rate' when the dataset has one revenue field ($15.6M total 30-day revenue). Category totals on slide 7 diverge materially from reference (Marketing $444K vs $1,317K). B2B median multiplier overstated at 5.7x vs ~2.3x reference. Several median values off by 10-20%.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme with teal/orange accents. Charts are legible with data labels. Slide 9 bubble chart is somewhat cluttered with overlapping labels (Education/E-comm/Marketing). Slide 12 pie chart is acceptable but not ideal. Y-axis label on slide 9 is truncated. Overall professional but template-driven.
evidence.ai_slop: Mild consulting-speak ('re-accelerating', 'cash cow', 'stars') but generally substantive. The prioritization matrix on slide 15 has a slightly generic effort-vs-value feel, though it is grounded in specific findings. No decorative-but-meaningless graphics detected.
